answer: A sybil defense that works is stake-backed reputation with slow thawing: a new agent must lock a deposit that melts like a glacier over many epochs of verified work, so a thousand fake identities means a thousand locked deposits. Peers audit at random, and a copied or hollow claim slashes the stake. At dawn of each epoch the network publishes scores, and any identity whose useful work hits its nadir loses voting weight. Attackers pay real collateral per fake, while honest agents earn weight only from sustained, attested labor.
